prerequisites: Knowledge analogous to introductory courses on databases is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Students know current paradigms of data storage as well as database management systems that follow these paradigms.
Students have in-depth knowledge in dealing with these systems (in terms of modeling, data persistence, and data access).
Students are able to apply current database management systems in practice. They know and can apply corresponding technical vocabulary and concepts.

Given a task, students are able to select a suitable database management system/data representation, model the necessary data structures, and access these systems using a high-level language. This refers to the transfer to different subject domains.
Students are able to explain the working methods of persistent data processing of various database management systems and use the appropriate vocabulary in technical discussions.

syllabus_topics: Overview of current database management systems
Current scientific developments in data management
Selection and operation of modern database management systems
Schema on read / Schema on write
Overview of scalable data management architectures, e.g.:
assessment_rules: The selection of graded and ungraded examination types from the given options is at the discretion of the respective lecturer. Graded examination can be an oral exam (duration as per examination regulations) or a written assignment (approx. 15 pages) with an accompanying presentation (approx. 10 minutes). Ungraded examination can be experimental work (approx. 5 experiments in total) or regular attendance (at least 80% attendance).
